competitive_landscape: Served entirely by conventional ferry operators (Bintan Resort Ferries, Sindo Ferry, Batam Fast) on fixed diesel schedules. There is no premium, on-demand, or foiling option — the volume is enormous and the experience is undifferentiated, which is precisely the opportunity.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Both crossings — Batam ~12 nm and Bintan ~30 nm — sit inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope with margin for multiple rotations.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Not needed for the crossings; Quanta-LR extends the network to the outer Riau (Anambas, Natuna) if it grows.

grab.note: Grab phase-2 cross-border anchor (Indonesia side): the 350k+/yr Lagoi resort flow and the high-frequency Batam shuttle — the in-app water tier on SEA's densest crossing.

regulatory_note: Cross-border Singapore↔Indonesia service runs through established CIQ ferry terminals (Tanah Merah, HarbourFront ↔ Bandar Bentan Telani, Batam Centre/Sekupang/Nongsa). Touches Singapore MPA clean-harbour-craft rules and Indonesian maritime/immigration.
seasonality: The strait is relatively sheltered year-round; the NE monsoon (Nov–Mar) brings occasional swell and ferry delays — conditions where foiling's smoother ride and reliability become the premium.

signature_routes.label: Singapore (Tanah Merah) ↔ Bintan / Lagoi resorts (cross-border, all-electric)
Dense Singapore ↔ Riau boarding-point mesh (17 BPs)

summary: The Riau Islands sit just across the strait from Singapore, and Bintan is the destination that matters: the Lagoi/Bintan Resorts coast draws 350,000+ international tourists a year (Banyan Tree, Club Med, The Sanchaya), reached today only by scheduled ferry to Bandar Bentan Telani. Batam is the high-frequency commuter-and-business crossing. Together they are the densest cross-border maritime corridor in Southeast Asia — and entirely un-premiumised.
tagline: Singapore's resort backyard — millions cross the strait every year, all on slow ferries.
